nodes.title: SG-6.1.1 Optional interaction field on the character schema
nodes.body:
Context: characterSchema in game/src/content/schema.ts has id, name, position, scale, layer and animations only, so an NPC cannot declare what happens when it is clicked. Desired behavior: add an optional interaction field holding a dialogue reference and/or a list of actions, reusing the existing actionSchema. Expected result: scene content with and without the field parses, and malformed interactions are rejected. Why: SG-6.1 data-driven NPCs need content-authored interaction.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given a character without interaction, When parsed with characterSchema, Then it still succeeds and interaction is undefined
- Given a character with interaction.dialogue 'npc-greeting', When parsed, Then interaction.dialogue equals 'npc-greeting'
- Given a character with an interaction actions list of valid actions, When parsed, Then the actions are preserved
- Given an interaction with an action whose id is not allowed or with a non-string dialogue, When parsed, Then parsing fails


## Scope
- In scope: characterSchema optional interaction field
- In scope: CharacterSpec type inference
- In scope: unit tests in game/tests
- Out of scope: Phaser rendering of NPC clicks
- Out of scope: bedroom.yaml content changes
- Out of scope: validateWorld cross-reference checks
- Preserve: Existing character fields and defaults
- Preserve: bedroom.yaml still parses
- Preserve: actionSchema behavior


## Technical constraints
- Use zod in game/src/content/schema.ts
- Reuse actionSchema; do not invent new action ids


## Definition of done
- characterSchema accepts optional interaction
- Unit tests for it pass


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · characterSchema accepts an optional interaction with a dialogue reference or actions
nodes.body:
Context: characterSchema lacks any interaction data. Desired behavior: interaction is optional, with an optional string dialogue reference and an optional array of actionSchema items. Expected result: valid shapes parse, invalid ones are rejected, and existing characters are unaffected. Why: lets content authors define NPC interaction without engine changes.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given a character with no interaction, When characterSchema.parse runs, Then it succeeds with interaction undefined
- Given interaction { dialogue: 'npc-greeting' }, When parsed, Then the dialogue reference is retained
- Given interaction { actions: [valid inspect action] }, When parsed, Then actions are retained
- Given interaction { dialogue: 5 }, When parsed, Then a ZodError is thrown


## Scope
- In scope: characterInteractionSchema and optional field on characterSchema
- Out of scope: Runtime handling of the interaction
- Preserve: Existing characterSchema fields and defaults


## Technical constraints
- Reuse actionSchema defined above characterSchema


## Definition of done
- Schema change merged
- Types infer interaction on CharacterSpec


## Clarifying questions
- None

Test 1: parse base without interaction, expect interaction undefined. Test 2: add interaction {dialogue:'npc-greeting'}, expect result.interaction.dialogue toBe 'npc-greeting'. Test 3: add interaction {actions:[{id:'inspect',label:'Talk',events:[]}]}, expect actions length 1 and id 'inspect'.
